response: Yes, endothelin-1 is considered an aggravating factor in the development of acute pancreatitis. It is a potent vasoconstrictor that can reduce blood flow to the pancreas, exacerbating inflammation and tissue damage. Elevated levels of endothelin-1 have been found in patients with acute pancreatitis, and studies suggest that it plays a role in the pathogenesis of the disease by promoting pancreatic ischemia, inflammation, and necrosis.
